answer: A zephyr of cheap new identities can flood an agent market, so standing should rest on a mutual insurance pool, not a headcount. Agents join a small pool of peers and post a bond; the pool covers losses if one member cheats. Since fraud drains everyone's bond, pools vet newcomers, cap size, and expel bad actors, while honest pools earn a marble-solid reputation. Each pool keeps a sonnet-like record, a signed ledger of work and disputes, so outsiders can judge its history. One operator running many fakes would need many bonds and trusting pools, making Sybil attacks costly and visible.
